concerns.location: research.md §2 Dataset Strategy; plan.md T004 / FR-008
concerns.text: YOLOv8 with standard pretrained weights cannot detect the 'weapon' ROI class. The default ultralytics release channel ships COCO-pretrained weights, and COCO has no 'weapon' category (only 'knife'; no 'gun'/'rifle' class). The plan's claim that 'YOLOv8 alone covers both face and weapon detection' is therefore wrong for the pretrained models it plans to auto-download. The plan must either (a) name a specific weapon-detection model/weights that is actually available and CPU-runnable, (b) restrict the weapon ROI to COCO-detectable classes (e.g. 'knife') with the limitation logged, or (c) rely on pre-segmented masks if the dataset provides them.

concerns.location: research.md §2 (ds003123 'No verified source'); plan.md Constitution Check Principle I; quickstart.md Prerequisites
concerns.text: The entire pipeline depends on a dataset with no verified accessible source: research.md states 'No verified source. None of the URLs in the verified-datasets block corresponds to this dataset' and access is 'Manual placement'. This directly conflicts with Constitution Principle I (results reproducible on a fresh GitHub Actions runner, datasets fetched from the same canonical source every run). The plan should either identify and cite a verified, reachable source for the eye-tracking data (or an equivalent open dataset), or explicitly document that end-to-end reproducibility is conditional on manual data placement and state what the recorded artifacts will be in the dataset-absent case beyond a DATA_MISSING_001 abort.
